subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose a generic Gateway receive timestamp to agents, and if so what stable field name, timestamp format, and metadata surface should become the public contract?
rationale: The missing source path is clear, but automation should not choose an agent-visible and plugin/SDK-adjacent contract name or representation without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt generic ingress timing metadata
options.body: Add one stable receive-time field across the shared inbound context and agent-visible metadata, backed by tests and docs for channel/plugin authors.

options.title: Keep timing internal/telemetry-only
options.body: Use logs or telemetry for latency diagnosis and leave agent-visible inbound metadata unchanged.

options.title: Defer to channel-specific instrumentation
options.body: Let each channel/plugin expose timing details independently, accepting that latency semantics may differ by transport.

recommendation.title: Adopt generic ingress timing metadata
recommendation.body: Add one stable receive-time field across the shared inbound context and agent-visible metadata, backed by tests and docs for channel/plugin authors.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has substantial feature-history ownership in inbound metadata and is the strongest product-contract routing candidate among the history signals.
